title: Chapter 176: Remember It
html:
The red of the girl’s dress made her face appear even more ethereal. Her black hair stirred in a wind Chen Ge could not feel. Zhang Ya stood less than thirty centimeters away. Cold seeped through his skin, turning his lips purple.

Fear curled around the heart of a man who feared almost nothing. He instinctively tried to lean back, only to discover that he could not move. The candy marked with a crying face seemed to dissolve into a river of ice, freezing every blood vessel in his body.

A wailing spirit surged through him. Negative energy gathered around his heart, constricting it like a pair of invisible hands. The candy refused to go down, and the lack of air left Chen Ge on the verge of fainting.

Radiating bitter cold, Zhang Ya drifted closer and finally stopped before him. Her bloodless face possessed a beauty so arresting that it caught the breath in his throat.

He could not utter a sound. As the candy melted, he felt a spirit roiling through his body. Zhang Ya’s face hovered barely six centimeters from his own, and his calves began to tremble uncontrollably.

This is not what I had in mind! Someone stop her!

Perhaps the Specter’s Favored title truly did work, because the monster blinded by the Pen Spirit suddenly charged him at full speed. Its narrow body slithered like a giant snake. Bony hands seized Chen Ge’s shoulders, and its lower half coiled as though preparing to spring onto his back.

Pain jolted Chen Ge from his fearful trance. He glanced over his shoulder and gave the monster a look of heartfelt gratitude.

Appreciation?

The reaction appeared to offend it. Its lofty head flew into a frenzy. With no intention of challenging Zhang Ya, it chose a spot on Chen Ge’s neck and lunged. Its distorted human jaws opened wide, only to halt half a meter from him.

It had not stopped willingly. Strands of blood-dark hair had wrapped around its body in the gloom. The monster shrieked and glared at Zhang Ya with naked hatred. It had ignored her earlier, but not because it feared her.

The three monsters exchanged some silent signal and shifted their attention to Zhang Ya. Chen Ge had no idea what she intended to do, but he saw her expression darken. Black hair bored into the nearest creature. Her slender hands seized its head and smashed it against the wall.

The monster wailed for only the second time that night. The first had been when Chen Ge drove the Pen Spirit’s pen into its eye.

This is so cruel.

Once Zhang Ya began fighting, the cold gripping Chen Ge eased enough for him to move. He hastily retreated. As the candy continued to dissolve, the spirit’s screams within him faded. Frosty energy gathered around his eyes, sharpening his sight once more until the darkness became clearer.

The three creatures closed in on Zhang Ya. Her red dress blazed in the dark, an embodiment of her seething rage and resentment. She looked ready to tear the monsters apart and devour them.

Ten minutes later, the corridor had become a slaughterhouse. The monsters accumulated wound after wound. They were strongest while fused with their human hosts; detached, their power diminished drastically. Even with superior numbers, they could do nothing against Zhang Ya.

The difference in power is so huge?

The lanky creature was the most terrifying ghost Chen Ge had ever encountered. He had initially assumed it might rival Zhang Ya, but he had clearly underestimated her.

There’s a reason the black phone gave her a page of her own.

Chen Ge tightened his grip on the cleaver, unwilling to lower his guard.

Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy could have been rated three stars at most, and Chen Ge suspected it was only a two-star scenario. Yet Zhang Ya, a ghost from that school, dispatched creatures from the three-star Third Sick Hall with ease. That could mean only one thing: something far more frightening than the lanky monsters was hiding in the hospital.

The black phone rated the Third Sick Hall three stars for a reason. There must be a Red Specter here—perhaps more than one.

The more Chen Ge considered it, the less sense the situation made. The door had stood open for years. In theory, the entire hospital should have become a nest of monsters by now. Did all the ghosts leave, or did something happen to them after they emerged from the world behind the door?

Glancing around, Chen Ge saw that the blood vessels from the first-floor corridor had spread to the fourth. They were creeping silently toward Zhang Ya.

This is bad.Chen Ge had regained complete control of his body. Zhang Ya’s candy had been made from a human soul, and its power had frozen him. Now that it had fully dissolved, the Yin Yang Vision absorbed its essence. Zhang Ya had never intended to harm him with it.

Something else is hiding in the Third Sick Hall. Maybe the building itself is the real monster!Chen Ge rushed forward, but after only a few steps, Doctor Gao’s voice sounded from the phone in his pocket.

“Chen Ge! I found Men Nan!” The call had remained connected, and what Doctor Gao had overheard made the urgency of the situation clear.

“Good. Put him on.” Chen Ge stopped. Men Nan was the key to everything—he had seen this door before and managed to close it.

“This is Men Nan, thank you for helping me last time…”

“Forget the formalities. There’s a child persona hidden inside your mind, and you should know how to wake him!” Chen Ge was running out of time. Zhang Ya’s appearance had begun to awaken the truly terrifying presence inside the Third Sick Hall.

“You must be mistaken. What other persona are you talking about?”

“He’s inside you!” Chen Ge raised his voice. “You were raised in a mental hospital. I don’t know how that affected your development, and perhaps you’ve tried to bury it, but some things can’t be escaped simply by pretending they never happened!”

“What are you talking about?” Men Nan did not sound as though he was lying. “Maybe I did grow up in a mental hospital, but who remembers anything from infancy?”

“An infant’s synapses develop rapidly, which can make recorded memories unstable. That’s why most people remember nothing from that period,” Doctor Gao explained in a clinical tone. “But those memories may not be completely gone. They could remain buried deep in the mind. If we can evoke them, perhaps we can awaken the childhood persona.”

“Evoke the memory?” Chen Ge searched his pocket and pulled out the photograph from the director’s office. He took a picture of it and sent it to Doctor Gao. “Men Nan, look carefully. This is the room where your mother stayed—Room 3 in the Third Sick Hall. Focus on the door that stood between you and her!”
